headline: New law changes how the VA repays veterans whose benefits were misused by a fiduciary handling their money.
what_it_does: When a fiduciary (a person appointed to manage a beneficiary's VA benefits) misuses that money, the VA can reissue the lost benefits. This law says the VA cannot hold back those repayments while it decides whether its own negligence played a role. The VA must set up methods and timelines for making those negligence decisions, but it does not have to make one for every case of misuse. If the beneficiary dies before being repaid, the money goes to a survivor, the same way some other VA benefits are paid after a death.

who_it_affects.group: Veterans and other VA beneficiaries who have a fiduciary manage their benefits
who_it_affects.how: If their fiduciary misuses their benefits, their repayment cannot be delayed while the VA reviews whether it was negligent.
They can receive reissued benefits that were owed to a beneficiary who died before being repaid.
It must create methods and timelines for deciding whether misuse cases resulted from its own negligence.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted December 12, 2025; the summary does not state a separate effective date.
